records.context: **The pyramid.** ``levels=1`` writes level 0 alone; more builds each level by halving the two fastest-varying space axes of the one above with a 2x **block mean** (``downsample="mean"``) or by **striding** (``downsample="stride"``). Neither is a Gaussian pyramid — there is no pre-filter beyond the box — and the block mean is the default because striding aliases: a one-pixel-wide bright structure survives or vanishes with the parity of its coordinate, so the same object appears and disappears as a user zooms. **Label and mask arrays must use** ``downsample="stride"``: the mean of labels 3 and 5 is 4, which is a different object, and averaging a boolean mask invents half-membership. Levels shrink by ``ceil(n / 2)``, so nothing is cropped off an odd edge.

Neither is a Gaussian pyramid — there is no pre-filter beyond the box — and the block mean is the default because striding aliases: a one-pixel-wide bright structure survives or vanishes with the parity of its coordinate, so the same object appears and disappears as a user zooms. **Label and mask arrays must use** ``downsample="stride"``: the mean of labels 3 and 5 is 4, which is a different object, and averaging a boolean mask invents half-membership. records.translation: **La pirámide.** ``levels=1`` escribe solo el nivel 0; con más niveles, cada nivel se construye reduciendo a la mitad los dos ejes espaciales de variación más rápida del nivel superior mediante una **media por bloques** 2x (``downsample="mean"``) o mediante **submuestreo por pasos** (``downsample="stride"``). Ninguno de los dos es una pirámide gaussiana — no hay prefiltro más allá del bloque — y la media por bloques es la opción predeterminada porque el submuestreo por pasos produce aliasing: una estructura brillante de un píxel de ancho sobrevive o desaparece según la paridad de su coordenada, de modo que el mismo objeto aparece y desaparece cuando el usuario hace zoom. **Las matrices de etiquetas y de máscaras deben usar** ``downsample="stride"``: la media de las etiquetas 3 y 5 es 4, que es un objeto diferente, y promediar una máscara booleana inventa una pertenencia a medias. Los niveles se reducen con ``ceil(n / 2)``, así que no se recorta nada de un borde impar.

records.translation: Devolver exactamente ``False`` detiene el barrido y devuelve las filas completadas hasta el momento; cualquier otro valor (incluido ``None``) continúa. Entre puntos es la única granularidad segura — un ajuste es atómico — así que una cancelación se atiende después del ajuste en curso, no durante él. La función de retorno de llamada se ejecuta en el hilo que llama, en línea; no debe bloquear, y una función de retorno de llamada que lanza una excepción aborta el barrido en lugar de ser silenciada, porque un notificador de progreso roto es un error del código que llama y ocultarlo dejaría el barrido en marcha sin nada que lo vigile.

records.context: Editing is allowed only when all five checks pass. 1. :func:`spacr.qt.preferences.get_db_browser_editable` is enabled in Preferences; it is off by default and is not on this screen. 2. This session explicitly selected the database with ``set_database(..., explicit=True)``. 3. The user selected "Edit mode" *and* confirmed it; selection alone does nothing. 4. The row has ``rowid`` or a primary-key identifier. Otherwise refuse the edit: matching column values could silently update many measurement rows. Before writing, probe ``COUNT(*)`` and roll back unless ``rowcount == 1``. 5. The text converts to the declared column type. SQLite accepts ``'abc'`` in an INTEGER column, but :func:`coerce_for_column` must refuse it.
records.label: spacr.qt.screens.db_browser#14
records.source: 1. :func:`spacr.qt.preferences.get_db_browser_editable` must be on — it is off by default and lives in Preferences, not on this screen. 2. The database must have been chosen explicitly in this session (``set_database(..., explicit=True)``). 3. The user must tick "Edit mode" *and* confirm; ticking alone does nothing. 4. The row must be addressable by ``rowid`` or a primary key. Without one, the edit is refused — an UPDATE matching on column values can hit many rows, which on a measurements table is silent mass corruption. The write also probes ``COUNT(*)`` for the row address first and rolls back unless ``rowcount == 1``. 5. The typed text must be coercible to the column's declared type. SQLite will cheerfully store ``'abc'`` in an INTEGER column; :func:`coerce_for_column` refuses instead.
records.translation: 1. :func:`spacr.qt.preferences.get_db_browser_editable` debe estar activada — está desactivada por defecto y se encuentra en Preferences, no en esta pantalla. 2. La base de datos debe haberse elegido explícitamente en esta sesión (``set_database(..., explicit=True)``). 3. El usuario debe marcar "Modo de edición" *y* confirmar; marcar la casilla por sí solo no hace nada. 4. La fila debe poder direccionarse por ``rowid`` o por una clave primaria. Sin ninguna de las dos, la edición se rechaza — un UPDATE que coincida por valores de columna puede afectar a muchas filas, lo que en una tabla de mediciones es una corrupción masiva silenciosa. Además, la escritura comprueba primero ``COUNT(*)`` para la dirección de la fila y revierte los cambios a menos que ``rowcount == 1``. 5. El texto escrito debe poder convertirse al tipo declarado de la columna. SQLite guardará sin quejarse ``'abc'`` en una columna INTEGER; :func:`coerce_for_column`, en cambio, lo rechaza.

records.context: It is spelt ``_rowid_``, and that is load-bearing. Every spaCR object table declares a column called ``rowID`` — the laboratory microplate row, ``'r1'``, ``'r2'`` — and SQLite identifiers are case-insensitive, so a bare ``rowid`` resolves to *that column* rather than to the row id. The version this replaces asked for ``max(rowid)`` and got two things wrong at once on every real measurements database: it scanned the whole table to take the maximum of a text column (measured: 21 ms warm, 41 ms cold, on a 200 000-row table — precisely the ``COUNT(*)`` cost this method exists to avoid), and then ``int('r16')`` raised ``ValueError``, which is not a ``sqlite3.Error`` and so escaped the caller's handler into the Qt event loop. :mod:`spacr.predictions`, :mod:`spacr.foreign` and :mod:`spacr.data_manager` all carry a comment about this shadowing; this method had not got the memo.

records.context: The two robust constants are *not* interchangeable and the module refuses to pretend they are. 1.4826 (:data:`MAD_SCALE`) is ``1/Φ⁻¹(0.75)``, the factor that makes the MAD of a normal sample an unbiased estimate of its SD. A moving range is ``|x_i - x_{i-1}|``, the absolute value of a *difference* of two observations, so its scale is ``sqrt(2)·sigma`` and its median is ``sqrt(2)·Φ⁻¹(0.75)·sigma = 0.9539·sigma`` (:data:`MEDIAN_MR_CONSTANT`). Multiplying a median moving range by 1.4826 overestimates sigma by exactly ``sqrt(2)`` — 41% wider limits, which is the difference between catching a drift and not. Both constants are computed from ``Φ⁻¹(0.75)`` here for the same reason c4 is computed from the gamma function.
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.control_chart#14

A moving range is ``|x_i - x_{i-1}|``, the absolute value of a *difference* of two observations, so its scale is ``sqrt(2)·sigma`` and its median is ``sqrt(2)·Φ⁻¹(0.75)·sigma = 0.9539·sigma`` (:data:`MEDIAN_MR_CONSTANT`). Multiplying a median moving range by 1.4826 overestimates sigma by exactly ``sqrt(2)`` — 41% wider limits, which is the difference between catching a drift and not. Un rango móvil es ``|x_i - x_{i-1}|``, el valor absoluto de una *diferencia* de dos observaciones, por lo que su escala es ``sqrt(2)·sigma`` y su mediana es ``sqrt(2)·Φ⁻¹(0.75)·sigma = 0.9539·sigma`` (:data:`MEDIAN_MR_CONSTANT`). Multiplicar la mediana del rango móvil por 1.4826 sobrestima sigma exactamente en ``sqrt(2)`` — límites un 41% más anchos, que es la diferencia entre detectar una deriva y no detectarla. Aquí ambas constantes se calculan a partir de ``Φ⁻¹(0.75)`` por la misma razón por la que c4 se calcula a partir de la función gamma.

records.context: The obvious thing to write here is ``|x - mean| / sd > 3``, and it is the one thing this module refuses to do. spaCR object measurements are skewed and heavy-tailed by construction: ``cell_area`` is a positive quantity with a long right tail, ``pathogen_area`` is zero-inflated, an intensity ratio has a denominator that can approach zero. The mean and the SD of such a column are themselves dragged by the very objects they are supposed to find — one debris particle measured at 40× the median area moves the mean, inflates the SD, and so raises the threshold that was meant to catch it. The failure is silent and it gets worse the worse the contamination is: this is the *masking* effect, and it is the reason robust statistics exist.

records.translation: Lo obvio sería escribir aquí ``|x - mean| / sd > 3``, y es justo lo único que este módulo se niega a hacer. Las mediciones de objetos de spaCR son asimétricas y de cola pesada por construcción: ``cell_area`` es una cantidad positiva con una larga cola a la derecha, ``pathogen_area`` tiene inflación de ceros, y un cociente de intensidades tiene un denominador que puede acercarse a cero. El fallo es silencioso y empeora cuanto peor es la contaminación: este es el efecto de *enmascaramiento*, y es la razón por la que existe la estadística robusta.

records.context: The well-level test is **different from counting flagged objects**. ``flagged_share`` provides that count and answers another question: it finds a few *catastrophic* objects, such as a segmentation failure or dust measured as a cell, but misses a uniform shift. The well-level robust score finds the uniform shift but misses an isolated catastrophe. Both belong on the well frame because neither replaces the other.
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.outlier_model#29
records.source: So the well pass is emphatically **not** "the well contains many flagged objects". That statistic exists — it is reported as ``flagged_share`` — and it answers a different question: it finds a well containing a few *catastrophic* objects (a segmentation blow-up, a piece of dust measured as a cell) while being blind to a uniform shift. The well-level robust score finds the uniform shift while being blind to the isolated catastrophe. Both are on the well frame because neither subsumes the other.
records.translation: Así que el paso por pocillo **no** es, en absoluto, "el pocillo contiene muchos objetos marcados". Esa estadística existe — se informa como ``flagged_share`` — y responde a otra pregunta: encuentra un pocillo que contiene unos pocos objetos *catastróficos* (un fallo grave de segmentación, una mota de polvo medida como célula) sin ver un desplazamiento uniforme. La puntuación robusta a nivel de pocillo encuentra el desplazamiento uniforme sin ver la catástrofe aislada. Ambas están en la tabla de pocillos porque ninguna engloba a la otra.

records.context: The alternative considered and not taken is the Rousseeuw–Croux ``Sn`` (``1.1926 * med_i med_j |x_i - x_j|``), which is the statistically better answer: it has a 50% breakdown point, needs no symmetry assumption, and does not collapse on tied data. It is not used because the naive form is O(n^2) — unusable on the 10^5–10^6 object rows spaCR routinely produces — and the O(n log n) algorithm is a page of intricate code to maintain for a path that is only ever reached when the MAD has *already* collapsed. The mean absolute deviation has a 0% breakdown point and that is stated plainly rather than glossed: it is a stopgap that keeps a degenerate column from flagging its whole tail, not a robust estimator. If the fallback fires, the honest reading is that the column is not continuous enough for this test.

records.translation: La alternativa que se consideró y no se adoptó es el ``Sn`` de Rousseeuw–Croux (``1.1926 * med_i med_j |x_i - x_j|``), que es la mejor respuesta desde el punto de vista estadístico: tiene un punto de ruptura del 50%, no necesita suponer simetría y no colapsa con datos empatados. Si se activa este respaldo, la lectura honesta es que la columna no es lo bastante continua para esta prueba.
